title: Carrollton Democrats - Bridge Brigade - ALPHABET RESISTANCE
description:
Please JOIN US this Saturday, June 7th, 2025 for a FUN early evening of GOOD TROUBLE. We will be doing a little APLHABET RESISTANCE on a Bridge Brigade over a Carrollton Freeway. 

Photo is pic of BRIDGE on McCoy and PGBT, facing NE.  You see the Dental Office in the NE quadrant where we will gather before accessing the bridge.

"Alphabet Resistance Signs" will be used in our Bridge Brigade on June 7th (from 5-6 pm) at McCoy Road and PGBT. We will meet at this address 1601 E Trinity Mills Rd, Carrollton, TX 75006. It is a dental office - plenty of parking - easy access to the bridge where we will be displaying our signs and flags. We will do a practice run in the parking lot about how we will be using the signs before we move on to the bridge.

We created "LIBERTY" and "JUSTICE" that will be flipped. And companion sign " FOR ALL" to be included in the message. (And we can flip the "for all" to "NO KING" if we choose). 

In addition - we created "SAVE DEMOCRACY" to be flipped to "DEFEND RIGHTS".

Large Cloth Banners - 8' x 4' with lettering that will grab driver's attention have also been created for this event. They will be attached to PVC that can then be temporarily attached to the fence with bungie cords. Lots of effort - lots of work. And we be able to use them at our monthly Protests and Demonstrations.

Please bring flags to wave. If wearing a hat (recommended) – please be sure it won't blow off to traffic below.  If you have an air horn – that is fine too. In addition to easy access from the parking lot to bridge, the bridge has wide sidewalks - and concrete about 2½ ft tall - with fence on top - about 5½ ft tall total. You should be able to see lettering through fence - and not be worried the signs could fly off the bridge if dropped.

Check out our other Mobilize Events for more Resistance Activities and Monthly Meetings. Bring a friend! Please sign up for our emails through CarrolltonDemocrats@gmail.com and join our Facebook Group. https://www.facebook.com/share/g/18yRmop8qP/

title: Stop Austin’s ALPR -- PRESS CONFERENCE
description:
Show your opposition to Austin's AI Surveillance License Plate Reader Program.

Join Austin City Council Member Mike Siegel, Grassroots Leadership, Austin Justice Coalition, Hands Off Central TX, Indivisible Rosedale,  League of Women Voters, and Workers Defense Action Fund to say 

NO to ALPR in Austin 🚫 

Here's why:

⚠️ Dangerous for Civil Rights

ALPRs have been used by cops to stalk exes, by ICE for deportations, and to track abortion seekers across state lines.

Protesters, activists, and marginalized groups are especially vulnerable to surveillance and retaliation.

🔍 Mass Surveillance with Little Oversight

540+ cameras scan tens of millions of plates quarterly — tracking everyone, not just suspects.

Data is shared with state and federal agencies, opening the door to misuse for abortion bans, anti-immigrant laws, and political targeting.


🛑 Bad Tech, Bad Actor

Flock, the vendor, has a shady track record and ties to far-right funders.

If they go bankrupt, your location data can be sold as an asset.

🧾 Contracts Mean Little

Current “safeguards” can vanish with the next mayor or Council.

Once the surveillance infrastructure is in place, it’s hard to roll back.

💸 Wasteful Spending

Austin’s ALPR pilot cost $244K/year and scanned 75 million plates — but less than 0.02% resulted in matches.

In a budget deficit, this is not a smart investment. The system has not proven to reduce or solve serious crime.

title: Bystander Intervention De-escalation Training presented by SURJ MKE
description:
Now more than ever, it’s going to take community to keep each other safe and minimize harm. No one is born with these skills, it takes lifelong learning and practice to keep the tools in your harm reduction toolbox sharp. Whether you’ve attended workshops before or this is your first time, this is the space for you!

Bystander Intervention/De-escalation training will focus on ways to intervene in public instances of racist, sexist, anti-Muslim, anti-Semitic, anti-Trans, and other forms of oppressive interpersonal violence and harassment while considering the safety of all parties. The physical and vocal practice of various strategies is designed to change social norms and encourage people to find ways to interrupt violence and prevent further harm.

This workshop includes a learning segment of tips and strategies, how to document, knowing your rights as an intervener, and practice scenarios constructed on ways to show up and support a diversity of identities through an intersectional lenses, both as the intervener and the person experiencing harm.

title: Breakfast Briefing: 2025 Budget Breakdown with State Reps. Benham and Powell
description:
Welcome to budget season in the PA General Assembly. Phew, are we here already?

We’ve invited State Reps. Jessica Benham (HD-36, Allegheny County) and Lindsay Powell (HD-21, Allegheny County) to discuss it at length on Thursday, June 12 at 8:30 AM and would love if you’d join us. 

What’s up with the budget anyway?
—It’s due by the end of June. This doesn’t always happen, but we’re hopeful that it will

—There are two types of budgets passed each year: a General Appropriations bill and a Codes bill – we’ll discuss the difference

—After Shapiro’s budget address in February, House and Senate Appropriations committees held budget hearings, which turn into close-door negotiation sessions — we want to know what they’ve been discussing

—Lawmakers typically amend existing bills to fit into the scope of the House or Senate Appropriations committees’ budget legislation

With both Rep. Powell and Rep. Benham sitting on various committees, we’re certain they will offer insights into how legislators are progressing some key issues such as Medicare/Medicaid, transportation, housing, climate change and more.

We look forward to answering questions posted in the chat during this briefing. If you can’t make it or want to send us a question in advance, please email us at info@representpa.org.

This briefing will be hosted by Represent PA’s Executive Director, Erin Belitskus. 

To join, please RSVP through Mobilize to receive the Breakfast Briefing link. 

And don’t forget to invite your friends and neighbors to join by forwarding this RSVP. It only takes a minute!
